question.text: Referring to the Chapter 6 sensitivity illustration: if the Hurdle Rate on Fund ABC is INCREASED from 10% to 12%, what happens to the Incentive Fee payable to the GP, all else equal?

answer.text: Incentive Fee increases proportionally with the hurdle
Incentive Fee DROPS significantly because the threshold for excess return rises
Incentive Fee is unaffected; hurdle only impacts LP preferred return
Incentive Fee becomes tax-exempt under Section 115UB

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6 illustrates: at 10% hurdle, incentive fees are ~INR 21.35 lakh + 41.99 lakh (Y1+Y2). At 12% hurdle the same scenario drops fees to INR 6.35 lakh + INR 8.69 lakh. Higher hurdle = higher benchmark to cross = LESS excess return eligible for GP carry. The Trap: A reverses the source's direction; C ignores the waterfall mechanic that places hurdle ahead of incentive; D confuses the hurdle mechanic with tax pass-through under Section 115UB. Note: A higher hurdle does not change carry economics in isolation — it raises the bar that must be cleared before any GP carry accrues, so the LP receives more of the early profit layer.
